title: Be a Little Silly
html:
Good morning,

Jessi Lane Adams said, “If you’ve lost your enthusiasm, there’s no better place to find it than on a skipping excursion. And you might just find your lost youth as well!”

When did you last do something silly for no reason? A dance or a silly voice out of the blue?

As children, we skip, make faces, invent games and laugh at things that aren’t even jokes. Then, somewhere along the way, we start worrying about how we look to others.

We become sensible.

Responsible.

Busy!

Those things have their place. But if every moment has to be useful, it’s easy to forget how good it feels to be alive.

That’s what I like about Jessi’s suggestion. You don’t have to feel enthusiastic before you skip down the path. You just do something a little ridiculous and see what happens.

If skipping feels like too much, put on a song and dance badly in the kitchen. Pull a face at someone you love. Take the long way to the car because you feel like running for ten seconds.

My son asked me to stand with my arms open and slid across the kitchen floor into my arms for a hug. He came in hot, and it was awesome and funny. We even demonstrated it for Lauren - such fun!

And if you’re a big, burly man, you can skip where nobody can see you. I won’t tell.

This week’s MondayMotivator

Take yourself less seriously for a moment. A little silliness might help you remember that joy is still there, waiting to be invited in.

Prompt for the week

What’s one small, playful thing you could do right now purely because it would make you smile? Do it!

To your success!

Glenn
